title: One Primary Apartment Home Lease per Resident
content:
**Clause.** A resident may be the primary leaseholder on only one Larkspur apartment home lease at a time — a limit of 1 Apartment Home Lease per resident. A new application is accepted only when the customer holds no other lease in applied, approved, active, in default, eviction filed or vacated status. Leases that are denied, cancelled or closed do not count.

**Moves.** A move to another apartment home in the same community during a lease is a transfer under the Lease Term Agreement charter and never a second application. A move to a different community requires the current lease to reach closed first.

**Who the limit covers.** Co-signers and occupants who are not the primary leaseholder are outside this cap.

**Evidence.** Whether another lease is held, and in which status, is read from the company's lease records for the applying customer; it is a system record, checked before the application is accepted.

## Status of the customer's other lease

| Status of another Apartment Home Lease held by the same customer as primary leaseholder | Counts against the limit of 1 |
|---|---|
| Applied | Yes |
| Approved | Yes |
| Active | Yes |
| In default | Yes |
| Eviction filed | Yes |
| Vacated | Yes |
| Denied | No |
| Cancelled | No |
| Closed | No |

## Hypothetical cases

- A customer whose earlier lease at another community shows vacated and has not reached closed holds a lease that counts; a new application is not accepted.
- A customer whose only earlier lease shows closed holds nothing that counts; the limit does not stand in the way of a new application.
- A person listed only as an occupant on someone else's lease is outside the cap and is not holding a lease for this purpose.
